claim: Within the specified two-worker uniform singleton-rebate class, a rebate offsets the worst-case production complementarity margin exactly when 2r >= kappa; a cap permits that guarantee exactly when B >= kappa.
bounded_conclusion: This identifies an exchange-inequality repair mechanism and a worst-case spending threshold for the stated policy class. It does not establish a unique cause in a particular observed market, another policy class, financing, welfare, or employer-specific wage-wedge equilibrium.

preferred_mechanism.statement: Paying r for a singleton hire reduces the adjusted valuation cross-difference by 2r, which restores EX against every production complementarity no larger than kappa.
preferred_mechanism.distinctive_prediction: For the worst-case admissible valuation with complementarity kappa > 0, GS fails at r=0 and holds within this class when 2r reaches kappa; robust affordability requires B >= kappa.
causal_chain: A singleton-only rebate adds r to each one-worker bundle and zero to the empty and two-worker bundles.
The adjusted cross-difference falls by 2r and meets the two-worker EX inequality when 2r >= kappa.
EX implies GS demand; P7 supplies common-wage equilibrium for EX-adjusted bundle valuations.

alternatives.statement: Every valuation allowed by the information bound already satisfies EX, so a rebate is unnecessary for the robust guarantee.
alternatives.observable_implication: The worst-case admissible valuation should have GS at r=0 even when kappa > 0.

alternatives.statement: An employer-specific modular hiring payment alone can repair a strict EX failure.
alternatives.observable_implication: Adding a modular schedule should turn the strict two-worker witness into an EX valuation.

alternatives.statement: A particular observed market may already satisfy EX despite the loose upper bound kappa; the rebate could be redundant there.
alternatives.observable_implication: Observed firm values would satisfy EX and GS at r=0 even though the information class also permits non-EX valuations.

tests.preferred_prediction: For kappa > 0 the admissible witness v(1)=v(2)=0, v(12)=kappa violates EX and all-real-price GS at r=0.
tests.alternative_prediction: The same admissible witness satisfies EX and GS at r=0.
tests.design: Apply the exact P8 counterexample and P3 real-price necessity argument to the bound-saturating two-worker valuation.
tests.decision_rule: Distinguish baseline robust substitution if the witness is in the information class and strictly violates EX/GS without a rebate.
tests.finding: The witness meets the complementarity bound with equality and strictly violates EX and GS at r=0 for kappa > 0.

tests.preferred_prediction: The P8 strict witness remains non-EX under every modular transfer; the singleton-only rebate is nonmodular.
tests.alternative_prediction: A modular transfer repairs strict EX failure in that witness.
tests.design: Combine the P2 modular-invariance proof with the P8 strict counterexample.
tests.decision_rule: Distinguish modular repair if the exchange cross-difference is invariant to every modular term.
tests.finding: P2 proves the modular term cancels from every exchange comparison, so it cannot repair the strict two-worker violation.

tests.preferred_prediction: If an observed firm has a strictly positive production cross-difference near kappa, a sufficient rebate changes its EX status.
tests.alternative_prediction: If observed firms already have nonpositive production cross-difference, they satisfy EX before the rebate.
tests.design: This would require verified employer-specific bundle values or a direct pre-policy demand audit; the present work is a theory model with no such observed values.
tests.decision_rule: Distinguish only with verified employer-level baseline values or observed demand establishing which prediction holds for the particular market.
tests.finding: The paper proves a worst-case guarantee, not an attribution of observed market demand to the rebate. No employer-specific data are supplied.
